actions.justification: Mandatory first step per ATS/IDSA CAP guidelines. Establishes baseline hemodynamic status and identifies severity markers such as hypotension, tachycardia, or hypoxia.
Mandatory per ATS/IDSA CAP guidelines. SpO2 of 96% and RR of 20 warrant formal respiratory assessment to evaluate need for supplemental oxygen and severity classification.
Mandatory per ATS/IDSA guidelines — chest radiography is required to confirm CAP diagnosis and identify complications such as effusion or multilobar involvement.
MANDATORY action per ATS/IDSA CAP guidelines. CBC is essential to assess for leukocytosis/leukopenia confirming infection severity and guides risk stratification.
ATS/IDSA CAP guidelines recommend CURB-65 or PSI scoring to assess pneumonia severity and determine appropriate level of care (outpatient vs. inpatient vs. ICU).
Per ATS/IDSA CAP guidelines, blood cultures should be obtained before antibiotic administration to identify causative organism and guide targeted therapy.
ATS/IDSA guidelines require assessment of ICU admission criteria (major/minor criteria) to determine appropriate level of care and guide treatment intensity for CAP patients.
BMP provides electrolytes, BUN, creatinine and glucose - important for CURB-65 BUN component confirmation, renal function assessment before antibiotics, and overall metabolic status in CAP.
ATS/IDSA guidelines recommend sputum culture for inpatient CAP to identify causative organism and guide antibiotic de-escalation. Should be obtained before antibiotic administration.
Procalcitonin helps confirm bacterial etiology of CAP and can guide antibiotic stewardship decisions per ATS/IDSA guidelines.
ATS/IDSA CAP guidelines recommend urinary Legionella antigen testing for hospitalized CAP patients to identify atypical pathogens requiring targeted therapy.

Per ATS/IDSA guidelines for non-ICU inpatient CAP, beta-lactam plus macrolide combination is first-line therapy. Patient is hemodynamically stable without ICU criteria, making this the appropriate regimen. Prompt antibiotic initiation is time-critical.

Patient has CAP with fever, leukocytosis, and pleuritic chest pain. Beta-lactam plus macrolide has already been given. Per ATS/IDSA guidelines, respiratory fluoroquinolone (e.g., levofloxacin or moxifloxacin) is an alternative or adjunctive option for non-ICU inpatient CAP. Given ongoing symptoms and the need for adequate antimicrobial coverage, this is appropriate.

Patient has fever (38.6°C), tachycardia (HR 98), and infectious process. IV fluids support hemodynamic status and ensure adequate hydration during acute illness, consistent with supportive care recommendations in CAP management.
